evidence: Cic. Sen. 65: mōrōsī et anxiī et īrācundī et difficilēs senēs
terms.comment: From mōs: someone with his own ways, never satisfied; also peevish, morose (Lewis & Short).
Of persons, hard to deal with or to satisfy; its everyday sense is “difficult”.

terms.gloss: decisive (of a fever); as a noun, a literary critic
evidence: criticus m., a critic: Cic. Fam. 9.10.1; Hor. Ep. 2.1.51
terms.comment: As an adjective only a doctors’ term, “decisive”, in late Latin; as a noun, a scholar who judges texts and poets. It never means fault-finding.

phrases.latin: ūsque eō difficilēs ac mōrōsī sumus, ut nōbīs nōn satisfaciat ipse Dēmosthenēs
phrases.english: we are so hard to please and so critical that even Demosthenes does not satisfy us

phrases.latin: Nōlī tam mōrōsus esse; bene cantāvit.
phrases.english: Don’t be so critical; she sang well.

sources: Lewis & Short: morosus · Lewis & Short: difficilis · Lewis & Short: criticus
